chapter: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
title: Depression years and the Rhythm Club as hiring hall
summary: McRae and Chick Webb scuffled in the Depression, and the Rhythm Club was where musicians waited for calls and the union sent bands out.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Charlie for a while and that Chick was getting his band --
This was really the depression. Things were really bad. The band was just trying -- everybody -- Teddy Hill -- everybody was gigging around then, you know.
MR. WELBURN: Scuffling.
MR. MC RAE: Scuffling and really scuffling.
And I used to hang out with Chick. You know, I used to hang out with him because I liked him.
Because we would gig at night -- the guy will come by -- you go in the Rhythm Club, you know.
The Rhythm Club was a place for Black musicians to go during the day and the week -- everybody would call up there.
The union would call up there. See, the 802 would call up there and say, 'is so and so there, got a gig for him.' So, they would call up and, 'it's a job opened for so and so,' you know. And
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
they'd call up and get somebody who wanted a band. If the union didn't have it, they'd call -- "well, call the Rhythm Club," so and so and so.
Somebody will say, "we want a colored band to do so and so and so."
So, if they didn't -- (inaudible) the union couldn't put together (inaudible) nobody was on the floor down there, they'd call the union (inaudible). Get certain guys who have bands.
There were a lot of guys who had, you know, had gig bands -- they just put together there.
Say you wanted a band to play your wedding or something. You want us to come out to Long Island or Jersey City, and you want an 8-piece band or a 6-piece band, you'd call the Rhythm Club.
The union will say call the Rhythm Club. Call that number and ask for so and so, they'll get you a band.
Yeah, but you had to report it to the union --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
No, no.
You didn't have to?
No. The union would call you. At that time, they were trying to get the musicians work, you know.
They'd call up the union and sometimes the union -- and the (inaudible) delegate the call to the union, see. "Hey, we got a gig for so and so. Is he around here."
Then he'd go out and get the guys. Say, "Hey, you working tomorrow night?"
Sometimes I had two gigs. I'd say, "Yeah. You want to play with so and so? I'm working with so and so, you take this gig and I'll take this one."
